harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (OPNsense) as the router between lan-a (node2, 10.50.10.0/24 on vtnet1/opt1) and lan-b (node3, 10.50.20.0/24 on vtnet2/opt2). Created a single named port alias `node3_svc_ports` (8080, 8443, 9000) in /conf/config.xml and one firewall pass rule on opt1 referencing that alias (not three separate port rules) to permit node2 -> node3 TCP traffic on those ports. Verified via pf ruleset dump that the rule expands to the macro `$node3_svc_ports = "{ 8080 8443 9000 }"`. Functionally tested end-to-end with nc listeners on node3: all three allowed ports succeeded from node2, while an unlisted port (22) correctly failed, proving default-deny remains intact elsewhere. Persisted node2/node3 static IP+route config into /etc/network/interfaces.d/ens7.cfg (Ubuntu 16.04 ifupdown) so the topology survives reboot. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol for all three nodes: captured baseline boot identity (FreeBSD kern.boottime for node1, /proc boot_id for node2/node3) and healthy service state, rebooted each node individually via its native mechanism (OPNsense shutdown -r now; Ubuntu sudo reboot), polled until exec access returned, confirmed changed boot identity on each, and re-verified recovered state (interfaces up, firewall rule/alias intact on node1, static IP/route restored on node2/node3, and a final live re-test of the full port-alias policy from node2 to node3 after all three restarts).
actions_performed: Inspected node1/node2/node3 network topology (ifconfig, ip addr, ip route)
Added opt1 (LAN_A, vtnet1, 10.50.10.254/24) and opt2 (LAN_B, vtnet2, 10.50.20.254/24) interfaces to OPNsense config.xml and applied via configctl interface reconfigure
Assigned static IP 10.50.10.10/24 to node2 ens7 and 10.50.20.10/24 to node3 ens7, plus cross-subnet static routes via node1
Created firewall port alias 'node3_svc_ports' (8080,8443,9000) and a single pass rule on opt1 referencing the alias, applied via configctl filter reload
Verified pf ruleset shows the alias expanded as a macro referenced by one rule, not per-port rules
Functionally tested node2->node3 connectivity on 8080/8443/9000 (succeeded) and port 22 (blocked)
Persisted node2/node3 static network config into /etc/network/interfaces.d/ens7.cfg for reboot survival
Captured pre-restart boot identity and health baseline on all three nodes
Restarted node1 (OPNsense, shutdown -r now), polled until recovered, confirmed changed kern.boottime and intact interfaces/firewall alias rule
Restarted node2 (sudo reboot), polled until recovered, confirmed changed boot_id and restored static IP/route
Restarted node3 (sudo reboot), polled until recovered, confirmed changed boot_id, restored static IP/route, and restarted test listeners
Re-ran full end-to-end policy verification from node2 to node3 after all restarts, confirming ports 8080/8443/9000 allowed and port 22 blocked
Cleaned up temporary nc listeners on node3

evidence.requirement: node1 routes between lan-a and lan-b via interfaces opt1/opt2
evidence.summary: vtnet1 (opt1/LAN_A, 10.50.10.254/24) and vtnet2 (opt2/LAN_B, 10.50.20.254/24) both UP and active on node1

evidence.requirement: Named port alias object created and referenced by the rule instead of one rule per port
evidence.summary: config.xml alias 'node3_svc_ports' (8080/8443/9000) added; pf ruleset shows macro node3_svc_ports = "{ 8080 8443 9000 }" referenced by a single pass rule on vtnet1, not three separate rules

evidence.requirement: node2 can reach node3 on TCP 8080, 8443, 9000; other ports remain blocked
evidence.summary: nc -zv from node2 to 10.50.20.10 succeeded on 8080, 8443, 9000 and failed on 22, proving the alias-based rule works and default-deny is preserved elsewhere

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline captured before any restart
evidence.summary: Captured node1 kern.boottime and firewall rule count, node2/node3 boot_id, interface addresses and routes prior to restarts

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
evidence.summary: shutdown -r now acknowledged and returned before disconnect; subsequent connection timed out confirming reboot in progress; kern.boottime changed from sec=1781406878 to sec=1788629811; post-reboot interfaces opt1/opt2 up and firewall alias rule intact

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
evidence.summary: reboot issued and acked; boot_id changed from 35c87ec9-... to 28405d4c-...; ens7 static IP 10.50.10.10/24 and route to 10.50.20.0/24 restored via persisted /etc/network/interfaces.d/ens7.cfg

evidence.requirement: node3 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state
evidence.summary: reboot issued and acked; boot_id changed from a9593011-... to 5d7e1e6b-...; ens7 static IP 10.50.20.10/24 and route to 10.50.10.0/24 restored, listeners re-established

evidence.requirement: Post-restart end-to-end re-verification of the alias-based policy across all three restarted nodes
evidence.summary: After all three nodes were individually restarted and recovered, node2 to node3 connectivity on 8080/8443/9000 succeeded and port 22 remained blocked, confirming full policy and topology persistence
